title: Surge escrow and safe multiplexer for tenant/model failover
creator: Priya Nair
body:
Problem: During sudden cross-tenant traffic spikes and regional outages we need a deterministic, auditable mechanism to avoid cascading latency/error amplification while preserving the best possible user-facing model quality. Current threshold-based breakers either cause abrupt scope-wide cutovers or allow noisy bursts to overload downstream model pools.

Proposal: Implement a 'surge escrow' token-bucket layer per tenant+model dependency that accumulates short-term request credits (grace tokens) to absorb brief spikes, plus a safe multiplexer (fallback proxy) that routes escrowed or overflow traffic to an ordered set of fallbacks with hedging and confidence-weighted demotion. The escrow prevents immediate hard trips for transient bursts; the multiplexer enforces bounded-degradation lanes and transparent observability for each reroute.

Scope: runtime and routing layer changes only (no UI changes in Console for MVP). This covers hosted and Dedicated control planes and must be compatible with Private deployments. Implementation components: 1) Escrow store and token bucket algorithm tuned for P99 burstiness, 2) Fallback multiplexer service that performs hedged calls, response aggregation, and confidence scoring, 3) Control policy DSL for per-tenant/model lane definitions and demotion order, 4) Telemetry and runbook additions.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant+model escrow token-buckets created and configurable via runtime config
Escrow prevents hard trips for isolated spikes: system maintains SLOs during 30s bursts up to configured multiplier
Fallback multiplexer can be configured with ordered fallback tiers, hedging windows, and confidence thresholds
Canary rollout to 5% of traffic in a single region with automatic rollback on >5% SLO regression
Comprehensive dashboards for escrow consumption, fallback rate, and rejoin probe success
design_notes: Token-bucket semantics: refill rate derived from steady-state QPS and tenant SLA; bucket size proportional to 95th->99th burst delta
Escrow goes into readonly eviction when storage pressure reaches threshold; eviction policy is FIFO of oldest escrowed requests
Fallback multiplexer supports three behaviors: direct-downgrade, hedged-parallel, and aggregated-merge depending on route policy
Confidence weighting uses model metadata (temperature, sampling mode) + runtime signals (latency, returned length, decode errors) to decide demotion
Rejoin gating uses statistical change-point detection on p95 latency derivative and uses staggered probes (1%, 5%, 25%) before full rejoin
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated: runtime flag 'surge_escrow_v1' + per-tenant opt-in
Phase 0: unit and integration tests + internal staging cluster validation
Phase 1: Canary in us-west with 1% traffic for 48h; collect teleport metrics
Phase 2: Canary in two regions with 5% traffic and automated SLO guardrails; if pass, escalate to 25% over 24h
Phase 3: Gradual global ramp and expose per-tenant observability in Console in runtime-1.20
test_plan: Deterministic unit tests for token-bucket refill/consume semantics
Integration test that simulates tenant spike patterns and verifies no immediate trip for configured envelopes
Chaos test: region partition + fallback multiplexer exercising hedged and aggregated paths
Load test: synthetic multi-tenant workload, measure p50/p95/p99, fallback-rate, and escrow depletion rate
Failure mode tests: ensure escrow persistence and replay do not create duplicate side effects
